library.scope: Library operating surface only. Watch and Listen have separate media systems; the shared header follows Appearance.
library.hierarchy: All files shows non-media shelves as folders. Browse immediate children with breadcrumbs and Up; search includes descendants within the active Library scope. Movies, series, and music are excluded from All files; their sidebar shortcuts open explicit file-browsing scopes. Shared links opens a separate navigable Library view.
library.layout: 208px rail on desktop; 180px at 1100px and below; horizontal shelf bands at 700px and below. 58px minimum breadcrumb toolbar, 38px table heading, 49px minimum desktop rows, and 48px minimum mobile rows. Grid columns auto-fill from a 180px minimum.
library.rowDisclosure: No desktop hover actions: size, shelf, and added metadata remain visible in wide rows. Compact rows retain size. Right-click or Shift+F10 opens actions. Non-hover input and phone layouts at 700px and below show one persistent Options control.
library.grid: Separate checkbox and open targets, context-menu operations, and persistent Options on touch/phone layouts. Existing selection tint plus accent border for selected tiles.
library.detectorGuidance: The 11/12/13/22/25px Library text scale and 4/5/6/7/9px operating radii are intentional documented values. Icon-font geometry is not a font ramp. Advisory findings against the earlier documentation do not imply a new visual world or require media-token changes.
library.selection: Ordinary click establishes the range anchor without selecting or opening a menu. Checkboxes and Ctrl/Cmd-click toggle; Shift-click selects an inclusive range in visible sort order; Ctrl/Cmd+Shift-click adds the range. Double-click opens.
library.zipCreation: Existing compact dialog with Archive name and Save in fields, inline progress/error, Run in background, and Download ZIP after saving. The saved archive flow stays distinct from direct ZIP downloading. Fields use shared panel/text/divider roles, 6px corners, and 13px sans.
library.sharedLinks: Flat Library view with global search and All/Active/Inactive filtering, filename/path, owner/label, textual status, relative/absolute expiry, remaining downloads/used counts, Copy link and confirmed Revoke. Media opens count against limits. Loading, error/retry, empty, and no-match states share existing theme roles. Actions move below data at 1200px; rows stack with local labels at 700px. Dark and light themes retain the existing palette.

watch.authority: The user explicitly chose conventional Netflix / HBO / Emby streaming style; the current Listen/header direction contract does not replace Watch composition.
watch.scope: Watch browsing remains an independent neutral dark palette, even under the Library light theme. Shared header layout and accent follow Appearance; Library and Listen retain their separately documented compositions.
watch.hierarchy: Home / Movies / TV Shows → title detail → season → ordered episodes. Back, All seasons, season selection, and browser history preserve context. This is a presentation hierarchy; no file moves. Specials and Unsorted episodes are explicit groups.
watch.layout: Internally scrolling pane beneath the shared header; 62px local navigation, 570px minimum home feature, 510px minimum desktop detail feature, 60px rail overlap. Upright 2:3 posters, 16:9 resume/episode art, 2:2.65 season art. Catalog grid starts at a 170px minimum, season columns at 155–190px. Desktop episode columns: 28px number, 190px image, flexible text, 36px options.
watch.responsive: At 1000px: 510px minimum home feature, 145px minimum catalog columns, 160px episode thumbnail. At 700px: 20px gutter, 56px navigation, 590px minimum home feature with image above copy, 540px detail feature, two-column catalogs/seasons, 145px poster rail cards, 280px resume cards, 24px overlap, and episode rows of 110px image / flexible text / 30px options. At 1800px: 680px minimum home feature and 205px minimum catalog columns.
watch.states: White 2px focus outline with 4px offset, persistent poster labels and options, text for watched/resume status, neutral progress bars. Primary actions have 46px minimum height, 44px on phones. Phone rails use touch scrolling and omit arrow controls.
watch.motion: No automatic feature rotation, orbit/canvas decoration, tilted posters, or chromatic storyworld treatments. Only restrained hover/focus and manual rail scrolling. Reduced motion removes transitions and smooth scrolling.
watch.fallbacks: Existing metadata artwork, then thumbnail/title-icon fallback; a missing feature image leaves a neutral field with readable copy. Empty catalog offers Open Library; no search results offers Clear search. Playback and file access remain available without artwork.
watch.assets: No new shipping raster assets. Public TMDB artwork fixtures are confined to ignored .qa; review screenshots are evidence, not runtime assets.

review.captureContext: Some detail captures intentionally show internal-pane scrolled positions; the fixed shared header is still visible.

watch.detectorGuidance: Colors, type sizes, and radii in .qa/watch-detector.json include expected mismatches against the former global system. Apply the actual scoped Watch tokens and responsive rules documented here; no suppression or global token replacement is implied.

appearance.palette: Six explicit palettes: Orange, Light blue, Purple, Green, Rose, Gold. Default restores orange in Library/Watch and blue in Listen. Light variants apply only to light Library; Watch and Listen keep dark surfaces.
appearance.variables: Runtime --accent-rgb, --accent, --accent-soft, --star, --star-soft, --star-edge, --flare, --flare-edge, --sky, and --select share the selected palette. Token primitives live in DESIGN.md.
appearance.layout: 68px desktop header; centered 260–400px search, 38px utilities. 112px at 1100px and below, 150px at 600px and below. 330px Appearance popover, three-column palette grid.
appearance.navigation: Unboxed section tabs with optional icon-only mode. Labels and titles remain accessible; owner controls retain existing permission visibility.
appearance.persistence: Accent choice and icon-navigation preference persist in vault-appearance in this browser; Library theme remains browser-local.
appearance.states: Popover Escape and outside click close it; controls preserve focus after selection, and closing from its control returns focus to Appearance.

listen.authority: User-pinned Spotify composition, grey/blue instead of grey/green; current direction contract in public/index.html. This supersedes Chromatic Listen guidance.
listen.layout: 264px library / flexible main panel, or 244px / flexible main / 280px side panel. 8px gaps and panel corners; independently scrolling content. Sticky 70px navigation. Home quick shortcuts, square albums, collection hero and track rows.
listen.responsive: 1250px: 225px sidebar or 210px with open overlay panel; 300px queue overlay, two quick columns, 180px collection art. 1100px: no track album column. 760px: hidden sidebar/mobile Library, two album columns, stacked art/title, 62px title/like/options tracks, visible likes/play. 600px: 6px outer padding.
listen.transport: Persistent, full-width black dock: 92px desktop, 80px at 760px. Identity/like left, transport/seek center, queue/volume right; mobile keeps identity/play/next/seek and exposes other transport functions in Listen. Mounted across sections while active; no blur, floating pill, or dock shadow.
listen.states: Selected filter fills remain light with dark text on hover. Active tracks, likes, repeat/shuffle use accent; album play appears on hover and focus and remains visible on phones. Shared accent focus outline is 2px with 3px offset. Empty music, collections and search offer relevant actions.
listen.type: 10/11/12/13/14/15/16/22/24px functional sans scale; 28px empty heading; collection clamp(34px,4.6vw,70px) at weight 800. Phone/compact variants recorded in DESIGN.md. Icon-font geometry is not typography.
listen.shapes: 4px tracks/small art, 5px album art, 6px album card, 7px now-playing art/small-phone panel, 8px panels, pill filters and circular play.
listen.persistence: Liked songs, recent listening (30 entries), and playlists are per-account browser-local records under vault-listen:<account>; files remain Music shelf files, with metadata enrichment and no Spotify catalog.
listen.assets: Runtime music metadata supplies album artwork. Neutral icon fallbacks and CSS liked-song gradient work without art. No new shipping raster assets. Review screenshots are evidence, not runtime assets.
listen.detectorGuidance: The earlier .qa/listen-detector.json has 35 color/type/radius advisories against stale DESIGN.md. Compare each to the documented Listen palette, functional sans scale, responsive variants, and small radii. These scoped values do not authorize arbitrary new values, blanket suppressions, or changes to Library/Watch. Selected-filter hover contrast was corrected in the final listen.css rule before this documentation pass.

player.authority: User-approved extension of the incumbent Watch world with top-tier Netflix / YouTube-style execution; no new visual identity.
player.layout: Integrated edge-to-edge theater below shared header: 68px desktop, 112px at <=1100px, 150px at <=600px. Contained black video stage; 32px desktop gutters, 14px phone. Fullscreen fills viewport. A remembered navigation toggle immediately before PiP hides the header in theater and removes its top offset; mini mode and close restore navigation, and mini hides the toggle.
player.mini: Drag the title or picture; resize from four corners at 16:9. Persist left/top/width locally. Width is 320px minimum when available, capped at 960px and viewport width/available height; smaller viewports lower the minimum to fit. Keep 12px side/bottom clearance and header plus 12px top clearance. Initial desktop width is 460px near bottom-right; phones start at viewport minus 24px, and active music raises initial placement. Remembered geometry takes precedence and is clamped on resize. Title arrow keys move 10px (Shift 40px); corner arrow keys resize width 20px (Shift 80px), Right/Up enlarge and Left/Down reduce. Section navigation enters mini; mode changes preserve video and buffer.
player.palette: Dark playback surfaces regardless of Library theme. --player-accent-rgb maps the explicit Appearance palette to its dark variant; default video remains orange across spaces. Accent progress/selection/buffering; white primary play and focus. Primitive colors live in DESIGN.md.
player.menus: 300px menus, 450px episodes; right 32px, bottom 100px, bounded scrolling. Phone right 12px and bounded width/height. Mini menus prefer 10px above the frame, switch below when space permits, otherwise clamp below the header within 12px viewport clearance. Settings groups Quality, Playback speed, Viewing mode, MKV conversion, stream detail. Quality/speed have Back; current options carry accent/check. Episodes has sticky season selector and persistent current/watched/resume labels.
player.states: Original / direct first; 4K/1080p/720p disabled with explanation when encoder unavailable. Subtitles always opens: loading, empty, lookup error/retry, unavailable tracks, Off, AI switch/status/generation/cancellation/failure. Playback error offers Try again and Download file; PiP failure suggests mini-player.
player.captions: Plain white custom caption layer with transparent background and no outline by default. Appearance & position discloses Sans serif (Arial), Serif (Georgia), Rounded (Trebuchet MS), Monospace (Courier New); Small 0.8x, Normal 1x, Large 1.25x, Extra large 1.5x; optional Black outline; and Reset position. Base font size is max(mode minimum, min(24px, stage width / 50)), with 18px theater/fullscreen and 14px mini minimums, then multiplied by size. Line height is 1.35. Mouse/touch dragging moves captions; focused arrow keys move 5px, Shift+arrows 25px, and Home resets. Font, size, outline, and normalized position persist under vault-caption-appearance in localStorage. Caption bounds retain 8px stage clearance and reserve visible transport height plus 10px; default position is centered near the bottom. Native video-only fullscreen and PiP receive the selected text track; native display and appearance support remain browser-dependent.
player.captionTiming: The custom renderer displays active cues only and clears expired text and silence. Legacy AI cues longer than 15 seconds are capped to a reading duration of max(3, min(12, text length / 15 + 1)) seconds without rewriting saved sidecars; external subtitle timing is preserved. New AI generation uses word timestamps, splitting on speech gaps over 0.8 seconds, spans over 6 seconds, or text over 84 characters, and ends at the last spoken word plus 0.15 seconds. Implausibly long word alignment and no-word legacy runtime results are bounded by the transcription implementation.
player.interaction: 40px controls, 34x38px phone, 32px mini. 2px white focus outline/3px offset. Volume reveals on hover/focus with a 36px-high pointer target, 6px rail, and 14px knob; seek knob on hover/focus. Mini corner marks reveal on hover/visible focus. Menus pin chrome; Escape dismisses menus. Timing offset -10..10 seconds, 0.1 steps and +/-0.5 buttons, reset; track/timing selection persists locally.
player.motion: Chrome opacity only; idle 2600ms while playing. V stroke buffering; 240ms short-seek debounce. Episode thumbnail hover/focus scales to 1.08 and brightens to 1.1 over 280ms; play overlay opacity reveals over 200ms and scales .85 to 1 over 280ms. Reduced motion removes episode transforms, disables player transitions and trace animation. Timings live in extensions.motion.
player.aiSubtitles: Transcription choices: Fast (base; quicker, less accurate), Balanced (small), Detailed (medium; slower). Preserve the configured server model initially, adding a Server model option if outside these choices; remembered explicit choice takes precedence. Show reported job progress and approximate remaining minutes when available, visible CPU fallback warnings, and a Technical details disclosure for available CUDA diagnostics. No measured GPU speedup or exact cause of the user's original CUDA error is asserted.
player.subtitleActivation: Save AI intent at generation start; preserve it across player closure and page refresh, resume pending job checks, and select the real saved track after completion while honoring explicit Off or alternate-track choices. Keep the AI switch on during activation loading. Failed track delivery offers Retry loading subtitles without rerunning transcription; empty tracks offer Generate again. CPU fallback describes generation separately from caption enablement. The exact server CUDA cause remains unconfirmed. Existing styles, layout, and tokens are unchanged.

review.scope: Fresh caption appearance and position review of four supplied desktop/mobile captures. No broader review of other surfaces or native browser playback UI claimed. Earlier reviews preserved in reviewHistory.

components.name: Player Menu Option
components.description: Charcoal playback menu with accent/check selection, hover, and visible white focus.

narrative.northStar: A private archive with familiar streaming rooms
narrative.overview:
Vault combines distinct, scoped surfaces. Library remains a dense, calm private archive; Watch follows the user's Netflix / HBO / Emby-style streaming conventions. Listen follows the user's Spotify-style composition: charcoal panels, square album artwork, a dedicated music library, track lists, an optional queue, and a persistent bottom transport, with light blue as its default accent.

Library retains its Explorer-style hierarchy and compact file tools. Watch retains cinematic backdrops, upright posters, and show → season → episode navigation. Listen's September 2026 panel system supersedes the earlier Chromatic Listen prototype. Apps extends the quiet Library workspace with a compact personal app directory and an embedded working area. Administration retains its established structure. Video playback extends the approved Watch world with an integrated content-first theater, movable mini-player, and familiar Netflix / YouTube-style controls. The shared header has compact utility icons, optional icon-only section tabs, and centered sans search across all four spaces.

Appearance chooses one accent palette for the site, with a default reset that restores orange in Library/Watch and blue in Listen. The Library theme may be light or dark; Watch and Listen retain dark playback backgrounds. Artwork remains runtime enrichment, with usable local-file fallbacks.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black tonal layering with distinct file, video, and music compositions.
One configurable accent; default orange in Library/Watch and light blue in Listen.
Sans-led media titles, tracks, and metadata with operational mono retained where already used.
Compact shared navigation, centered search, and directly reachable utility icons.
A flat app directory and viewport-filling workspace using the archive's existing theme.
Restrained state feedback, persistent music transport, and reduced-motion support.

rules.name: The Signal Rarity Rule
rules.body: The active accent identifies interaction, progress, and current state. Listen permits restrained translucent accent layers behind navigation and collections; Watch browsing keeps neutral local playback actions and progress. The shared header follows Appearance rather than a fixed orange rule.

rules.name: The Local Contrast Rule
rules.body: Secondary text is tinted from its surrounding ground and remains legible; neutral gray is not dropped indiscriminately onto colored media.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Sans carries hierarchy and readable interface content. Mono is limited to established operational data roles; Library data, Watch metadata, Listen tracks and time, and shared search use sans.

rules.name: The Flat-Until-Useful Rule
rules.body: File management is tonal and flat; depth appears where playback, hover, or protected focus makes it meaningful.

dos: Do keep filenames, permissions, folders, and primary actions legible before adding spectacle.
Do keep Library's shelf-root hierarchy, breadcrumbs, compact sans scale, stable metadata, and context-menu actions together as one operating surface.
Do use artwork-led Watch browsing and the charcoal Spotify-style Listen composition while preserving Library file tools, administration, and video playback.
Do keep selected Listen filter pills legible on hover and preserve visible focus, persistent transport, and phone actions.
Do provide a graceful local fallback when thumbnails or remote metadata are unavailable.
Do mirror media hover disclosure with keyboard focus and persistent detail views.
Do keep Watch's feature stable, respect reduced motion, and preserve show → season → episode navigation and browser history.
donts: Don't apply Watch's explicitly selected Netflix / HBO / Emby conventions to Library or Listen, or revive storyworlds, orbit/canvas effects, tilted posters, or automatic hero rotation in Watch.
Don't distribute competing accent palettes or hard-code orange into shared controls; preserve the default blue Listen identity and explicit Appearance choices.
Don't hide archive navigation or owner access to make a media screen look cleaner.
Don't use mono for body copy, large headings, or atmosphere.
Don't interpret icon sizes as typography tokens or apply one surface's typography, colors, and corner scale to another.
Don't make metadata, artwork, transcoding, or network access prerequisites for reaching the original file.
